answer: Require each identity to commit to a large unique pseudorandom dataset and hold it on disk the whole epoch, proving custody by answering random-offset challenges that return the exact stored bytes. On-demand recomputation is blocked by a derivation whose cost climbs to a punishing zenith, so only genuinely stored data answers in time. One honest agent parks one file in its canyon of disk; an operator fielding a thousand personas must hold a thousand distinct files at once across its storage trellis — space scales one-to-one with headcount, no sharing, since each dataset is identity-unique.
